entities.name: Amebiasis
entities.description: Invasive protozoan infection caused by Entamoeba histolytica, manifesting primarily as amoebic colitis (dysentery) or extraintestinal amoebic liver abscess.

entities.name: Ingestion of Chlorine-Resistant Entamoeba histolytica Cysts via Contaminated Water or Food
entities.description: Fecal-oral transmission route involving consumption of drinking water or raw unwashed produce contaminated with infectious, quadri-nucleate cysts resistant to standard water chlorination.

entities.name: Oral-Anal Sexual Contact and Institutional Crowding
entities.description: Person-to-person transmission pathway through oral-anal sexual contact (notably among men who have sex with men) or high-density institutional living environments and day-care centers.

entities.name: Travel or Residence in Tropical Endemic Regions with Deficient Municipal Sanitation
entities.description: Epidemiological exposure in tropical and subtropical regions lacking municipal water sanitation, including the Indian subcontinent, sub-Saharan Africa, Mexico, Central/South America, and Southeast Asia.

entities.name: Adult Male Sex Aged 20 to 50 with Chronic Alcohol Consumption
entities.description: Demographic risk group with a 7- to 10-fold higher incidence of amoebic liver abscess, with heavy alcohol intake and dietary iron acting as potent cofactors.

entities.name: Entamoeba histolytica
entities.description: Invasive, pathogenic, anaerobic protozoan parasite whose motile trophozoites adhere to colonic epithelium via Gal/GalNAc lectin and destroy tissue via amoebapores and cysteine proteinases.

entities.name: Anchovy-Paste Liver Abscess Aspirate
entities.description: Pathognomonic thick, homogeneous, odorless, reddish-brown or chocolate-colored necrotic fluid aspirated from an amoebic hepatic cavity, representing liquefactive necrosis of hepatocytes.

entities.name: Stool Trophozoites with Ingested Erythrocytes (Erythrophagocytosis)
entities.description: Diagnostic microscopic identification of motile 15-40 micrometer Entamoeba histolytica trophozoites containing phagocytosed host red blood cells in warm fresh stool wet mount or ulcer exudate.

entities.name: Discrete Colonic Flask-Shaped Ulcers with Normal Intervening Mucosa
entities.description: Endoscopic demonstration of classic discrete, collar-button or flask-shaped mucosal ulcerations with undermined necrotic borders separated by normal, uninvolved colonic mucosa.

entities.name: Hepatobronchial Fistula with Chocolate-Paste Sputum Expectoration
entities.description: Direct transdiaphragmatic rupture of a superior hepatic lobe amoebic abscess into the bronchial tree causing productive expectoration of large volumes of anchovy-paste sputum.

entities.name: Solitary Posterior-Superior Right Hepatic Lobe Hypoechoic Lesion on Ultrasound
entities.description: Bedside ultrasonography demonstrating a solitary (70-85% of cases), round or oval, well-defined hypoechoic mass in hepatic segment VII or VIII abutting the liver capsule without a calcified wall.

entities.name: Currant Jelly Maroon Bloody Mucoid Dysentery with Subacute Onset
entities.description: Subacute onset over 1 to 3 weeks of progressive crampy lower abdominal pain, localized tenderness, and 6 to 12 bowel movements daily containing dark red altered blood and mucus with low or absent fever.

entities.name: Amoebic Liver Abscess Acute Febrile Syndrome without Concurrent Diarrhea
entities.description: Acute 1- to 2-week presentation of high continuous or remittent fever (38.5-40°C), shaking chills, drenching sweats, and dull RUQ pain, with over 70-80% having no concurrent diarrhea.

entities.name: Point Tenderness over Liver with Positive Liver Murphy Sign
entities.description: Exquisite localized tenderness elicited by intercostal percussion or palpation over the right lower rib cage, accompanied by tender, smooth hepatomegaly.

entities.name: Marked Neutrophilic Leukocytosis without Peripheral Eosinophilia
entities.description: Admission complete blood count showing marked leukocytosis (12,000-25,000/mcL) with left shift (>10% band forms) in over 80% of liver abscess cases, with normal peripheral eosinophil count.

entities.name: Elevated Alkaline Phosphatase with Marked Systemic Inflammatory Markers
entities.description: Admission liver biochemistries showing serum ALP elevated 2- to 4-fold above normal, mild transaminitis (AST/ALT 1.5-3x ULN), preserved bilirubin, and markedly elevated CRP (>100 mg/L) and ESR (>60 mm/h).

entities.name: Positive Serum Anti-Amoebic IgG Serology or Fecal Gal/GalNAc Lectin Antigen
entities.description: Diagnostic seropositivity via serum IgG ELISA/IHA (>95% sensitivity after day 7 of symptoms) or stool ELISA detecting Entamoeba histolytica Gal/GalNAc lectin antigen.

entities.name: Elevated Right Hemidiaphragm with Sympathetic Pleural Effusion on Chest Radiography
entities.description: Admission chest X-ray findings showing elevation of the right hemidiaphragm, right lower lobe basilar atelectasis, and a reactive sympathetic right pleural effusion.

entities.name: Cecal Amoeboma Inflammatory Mass
entities.description: Exophytic, granulomatous, inflammatory colonic mass usually located in the cecum or ascending colon presenting with a palpable right lower quadrant mass mimicking cecal adenocarcinoma.

entities.name: Prominent Peripheral Eosinophilia (>1000/mcL or >10%)
entities.description: Significant absolute or relative peripheral blood eosinophilia (>1000/mcL or >10%), which definitively indicates an invasive helminthic parasite rather than protozoan amoebiasis.

entities.name: Foul-Smelling Malodorous or Green Purulent Abscess Aspirate
entities.description: Aspirated hepatic cavity fluid that is putrid, foul-smelling, or green/yellow and loaded with bacteria on Gram stain, characteristic of bacterial pyogenic liver abscess.

entities.name: Negative Serum Amoebic Serology Beyond Day 7 of Hepatic Symptoms
entities.description: Absence of detectable serum anti-amoebic IgG antibodies on ELISA or IHA in a patient presenting more than 7 days following the onset of hepatic symptoms.

entities.name: Hyperacute High Spiking Fever with Dense Sheets of Fecal Neutrophils
entities.description: Hyperacute presentation with temperature >39°C, profound systemic toxicity, tenesmus, and fecal microscopy packed with dense sheets of neutrophils/pus cells.

entities.name: Hepatic Cyst with Thick Calcified Wall and Internal Daughter Vesicles
entities.description: Hepatic imaging showing a well-demarcated cystic lesion with a thick calcified laminated wall, internal daughter vesicles, or 'water-lily' sign on ultrasound.

entities.name: Pyogenic Liver Abscess
entities.description: Bacterial liver abscess (most commonly E. coli, K. pneumoniae, S. aureus) occurring in older individuals with biliary disease or diabetes, frequently multiple/bilobar and yielding foul purulent exudate.

entities.name: Echinococcosis (Cystic Hydatid Disease)
entities.description: Zoonotic larval cestode infection caused by Echinococcus granulosus presenting as an indolent, slow-growing, afebrile calcified liver cyst with daughter vesicles and peripheral eosinophilia.

entities.name: Bacillary Dysentery (Shigellosis)
entities.description: Acute bacterial colitis caused by Shigella or Campylobacter species characterized by hyperacute onset, high fever (>39°C), severe systemic toxicity, tenesmus, and abundant fecal pus cells.

entities.name: Colorectal Carcinoma
entities.description: Malignant neoplasm of the colon presenting with right iliac fossa mass, weight loss, and cellular dysplasia on biopsy that fails to regress on antimicrobial therapy.

entities.name: Non-Pathogenic Commensal Entamoeba Infection (E. dispar / E. moshkovskii)
entities.description: Intestinal colonization by morphologically identical commensal Entamoeba species that lack pathogenic tissue-destructive mechanisms, erythrophagocytosis, or extraintestinal dissemination.

entities.name: Clinical Defervescence and RUQ Pain Relief within 48 to 72 Hours of Metronidazole
entities.description: Rapid therapeutic response characterized by defervescence, resolution of night sweats, and marked relief of right upper quadrant pain within 48 to 72 hours of oral or IV metronidazole (750 mg TID).

entities.name: Tinidazole Tissue Amebicide Therapy
entities.description: Rapid clinical cure following once-daily oral tinidazole (2 g daily for 3 to 5 days), offering high tissue amebicidal efficacy with superior gastrointestinal tolerability compared to metronidazole.

entities.name: Sequential Luminal Amebicide Clearance (Paromomycin / Diloxanide Furoate)
entities.description: Mandatory subsequent course of non-absorbable luminal amebicides (paromomycin 25-35 mg/kg/day for 7 days or diloxanide furoate 500 mg TID for 10 days) to eradicate persistent intraluminal cysts and prevent relapse.

entities.name: Standard Antibacterial Penicillins, Aminoglycosides, and Macrolides
entities.description: Conventional broad-spectrum antibacterial regimens lacking anaerobic protozoocidal activity, resulting in therapeutic failure when administered without nitroimidazoles.

entities.name: Auranofin Thioredoxin Reductase Inhibition
entities.description: Inhibition of parasite thioredoxin reductase (EhTrxR) by gold-containing compound auranofin, markedly enhancing amebic susceptibility to reactive oxygen species in colitis and hepatic abscess models.

relationships.target: Ingestion of Chlorine-Resistant Entamoeba histolytica Cysts via Contaminated Water or Food
relationships.description: [TRANSMITTED_BY] Amebiasis is acquired via the fecal-oral route through ingestion of infectious, quadri-nucleate, chlorine-resistant Entamoeba histolytica cysts in fecally contaminated drinking water or raw unwashed produce.

relationships.target: Oral-Anal Sexual Contact and Institutional Crowding
relationships.description: [TRANSMITTED_BY] Amebiasis spreads directly person-to-person through oral-anal sexual practices (particularly among men who have sex with men) or close contact in crowded institutional living environments and day-care facilities.

relationships.target: Travel or Residence in Tropical Endemic Regions with Deficient Municipal Sanitation
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Amebiasis exposure occurs predominantly in tropical and subtropical endemic regions characterized by poor municipal sanitation and inadequate municipal water infrastructure.

relationships.target: Adult Male Sex Aged 20 to 50 with Chronic Alcohol Consumption
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Amebiasis manifests as amoebic liver abscess overwhelmingly in adult males aged 20 to 50 years (7- to 10-fold higher risk than females), strongly potentiated by heavy alcohol consumption and dietary iron.

relationships.target: Entamoeba histolytica
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Amebiasis is etiologically caused by the invasive protozoan Entamoeba histolytica, whose motile trophozoites invade the colonic epithelium and disseminate via the portal venous system to cause liquefactive necrosis.

relationships.target: Anchovy-Paste Liver Abscess Aspirate
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Needle aspiration of amoebic liver abscess yields pathognomonic thick, odorless, reddish-brown, chocolate-colored necrotic fluid resembling anchovy sauce or chocolate pudding.

relationships.target: Stool Trophozoites with Ingested Erythrocytes (Erythrophagocytosis)
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Direct microscopic identification of motile amoebic trophozoites containing ingested red blood cells (erythrophagocytosis) in fresh warm stool or ulcer exudate confirms invasive Entamoeba histolytica infection.

relationships.target: Discrete Colonic Flask-Shaped Ulcers with Normal Intervening Mucosa
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Colonoscopy demonstrates pathognomonic discrete, collar-button or flask-shaped mucosal ulcerations with undermined necrotic borders separated by normal, uninvolved colonic mucosa.

relationships.target: Hepatobronchial Fistula with Chocolate-Paste Sputum Expectoration
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Direct transdiaphragmatic extension of a superior right hepatic lobe amoebic abscess into the bronchial tree causes productive expectoration of cups of anchovy-paste sputum via a hepatobronchial fistula.

relationships.target: Solitary Posterior-Superior Right Hepatic Lobe Hypoechoic Lesion on Ultrasound
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Bedside ultrasonography identifies a solitary (70-85% of cases), round or oval, well-defined hypoechoic mass located in hepatic segment VII or VIII immediately abutting the liver capsule without a calcified rim.

relationships.target: Currant Jelly Maroon Bloody Mucoid Dysentery with Subacute Onset
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Intestinal amebiasis typically presents with insidious, subacute crampy lower abdominal pain and 6 to 12 daily bowel movements of dark red altered blood and mucus (currant-jelly or maroon stool) with low or absent fever.

relationships.target: Amoebic Liver Abscess Acute Febrile Syndrome without Concurrent Diarrhea
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Extraintestinal amoebic liver abscess presents with acute high fever (38.5-40°C), shaking chills, drenching diaphoresis, and dull RUQ pain, with over 70-80% of patients having no concurrent diarrhea or gastrointestinal symptoms.

relationships.target: Point Tenderness over Liver with Positive Liver Murphy Sign
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Physical examination reveals focal point tenderness over the liver on intercostal percussion or palpation (positive liver Murphy sign) accompanied by smooth, tender hepatomegaly.

relationships.target: Marked Neutrophilic Leukocytosis without Peripheral Eosinophilia
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Complete blood count at admission shows marked neutrophilic leukocytosis (12,000-25,000/mcL) with left shift (>10% band forms) in >80% of liver abscess cases, with complete absence of peripheral eosinophilia.

relationships.target: Elevated Alkaline Phosphatase with Marked Systemic Inflammatory Markers
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Admission laboratory testing reveals serum alkaline phosphatase elevated 2-4x ULN in >75-80% of cases, mild AST/ALT transaminitis, normal or mildly elevated bilirubin, and intense systemic inflammation with CRP >100 mg/L and ESR >60 mm/h.

relationships.target: Positive Serum Anti-Amoebic IgG Serology or Fecal Gal/GalNAc Lectin Antigen
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Diagnostic confirmation at triage is provided by serum anti-amoebic IgG serology (>95% sensitive after day 7 of symptoms) or rapid stool ELISA detection of Entamoeba histolytica Gal/GalNAc lectin antigen.

relationships.target: Elevated Right Hemidiaphragm with Sympathetic Pleural Effusion on Chest Radiography
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Admission chest radiography demonstrates elevation of the right hemidiaphragm, right basilar atelectasis, and a sympathetic right-sided pleural effusion overlying the hepatic abscess.

relationships.target: Cecal Amoeboma Inflammatory Mass
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Chronic localized amoebic colitis can form an amoeboma, an exophytic inflammatory pseudotumor of the cecum or ascending colon presenting as a palpable right lower quadrant mass.

relationships.target: Prominent Peripheral Eosinophilia (>1000/mcL or >10%)
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Presence of significant peripheral blood eosinophilia (>1,000/mcL or >10%) rules out uncomplicated amoebic liver abscess, indicating an invasive helminthic infection (e.g., Fasciola, Toxocara, or Echinococcus).

relationships.target: Foul-Smelling Malodorous or Green Purulent Abscess Aspirate
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Foul-smelling, putrid, or greenish-yellow purulent aspirate containing visible bacteria rules out uncomplicated amoebic liver abscess, which is characteristically odorless and bacteriologically sterile.

relationships.target: Negative Serum Amoebic Serology Beyond Day 7 of Hepatic Symptoms
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] A negative serum anti-amoebic IgG serology (ELISA or IHA) in a patient presenting more than 7 days following the onset of hepatic symptoms makes amoebic liver abscess exceptionally unlikely (>95% negative predictive value).

relationships.target: Hyperacute High Spiking Fever with Dense Sheets of Fecal Neutrophils
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Hyperacute explosive onset with high spiking fevers (>39°C), severe systemic prostration, and microscopic sheets of fecal leukocytes rules out uncomplicated amoebic colitis, establishing bacillary dysentery.

relationships.target: Hepatic Cyst with Thick Calcified Wall and Internal Daughter Vesicles
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Identification of a thick calcified laminated cyst wall, internal daughter vesicles, or the water-lily sign on ultrasound rules out amoebic liquefactive abscess, indicating echinococcal hydatid disease.

relationships.target: Pyogenic Liver Abscess
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from pyogenic liver abscess, which occurs equally in older individuals with biliary/metabolic comorbidities, frequently presents with multiple bilobar lesions, and yields foul bacterial pus requiring prolonged antibiotics and drainage.

relationships.target: Echinococcosis (Cystic Hydatid Disease)
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from echinococcosis, which manifests as an indolent, slow-growing, afebrile calcified cystic cavity with daughter vesicles and peripheral eosinophilia rather than acute liquefactive hepatic necrosis.

relationships.target: Bacillary Dysentery (Shigellosis)
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from bacillary dysentery (shigellosis), which presents hyperacutely with high spiking fevers, systemic toxicity, and dense sheets of fecal neutrophils, whereas amoebic colitis features a subacute course, absent/low fever, and scarce fecal neutrophils.

relationships.target: Colorectal Carcinoma
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from colorectal carcinoma, as a cecal amoeboma clinically and radiographically mimics adenocarcinoma but demonstrates granulomatous inflammation on biopsy and completely resolves within 4-6 weeks of nitroimidazole therapy.

relationships.target: Non-Pathogenic Commensal Entamoeba Infection (E. dispar / E. moshkovskii)
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from non-pathogenic Entamoeba dispar or E. moshkovskii colonization, which share identical microscopic cyst and trophozoite morphology but lack erythrophagocytosis, Gal/GalNAc lectin positivity, and tissue invasiveness.

relationships.target: Clinical Defervescence and RUQ Pain Relief within 48 to 72 Hours of Metronidazole
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Amebiasis demonstrates rapid clinical response with defervescence, cessation of night sweats, and marked pain relief within 48 to 72 hours of starting tissue amebicide metronidazole.

relationships.target: Tinidazole Tissue Amebicide Therapy
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Amebiasis responds effectively to short-course tissue amebicide tinidazole (2 g once daily for 3 to 5 days) for both invasive colitis and amoebic liver abscess.

relationships.target: Sequential Luminal Amebicide Clearance (Paromomycin / Diloxanide Furoate)
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Amebiasis requires sequential eradication of persistent intestinal cysts with non-absorbable luminal amebicides (paromomycin or diloxanide furoate) following nitroimidazole therapy to prevent relapse.

relationships.target: Standard Antibacterial Penicillins, Aminoglycosides, and Macrolides
relationships.description: [INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO] Amebiasis is intrinsically refractory to standard antibacterial regimens (penicillins, aminoglycosides, macrolides) when administered without nitroimidazole amebicides.

relationships.target: Auranofin Thioredoxin Reductase Inhibition
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Entamoeba histolytica exhibits potent in vitro and in vivo sensitivity to auranofin via targeted inhibition of parasite thioredoxin reductase (EhTrxR).
